appraisal_events.evidence: « je n’eus qu’à me rappeler qu’elle ne m’avait pas même offert d’aller voir les Elstir » ; « je savais que je ne lui plaisais pas, que je n’avais pas à espérer me faire aimer d’elle »
appraisal_events.explanation: Against Saint-Loup's report that his aunt feels shunned, the narrator produces the withheld invitation to see the Elstirs as proof that Mme de Guermantes does not care for him; the narrator endorses this as settled knowledge of his own exclusion from her favour.

appraisal_events.evidence: « elle était avec moi d’un empressement… dicté par la crainte qu’elle avait de faire fâcher ce fils… sur lequel elle croyait donc que l’empire qu’elle exerçait n’égalait pas et devait ménager le mien »
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme de Marsantes courts the narrator anxiously because she believes his hold over Robert exceeds her own, which locally credits him with leverage over both mother and son; his discomfort qualifies the position without cancelling the advantage.

status_effects.explanation: He is confirmed as unwanted by Mme de Guermantes, who did not even offer him the Elstirs, so he leaves for Balbec outside her circle of favour.
Mme de Marsantes' fearful eagerness places him in the stronger position, as the person whose influence over Robert must be managed.
She is shown dependent and placating, conceding that her empire over her son is weaker than a guest's and impatient for a private moment she does not control.

ambiguities: In Bloch's imagined remark « Dire que pour une fois il n’avait pas menti, c’est incroyable », the referent of « il » is underdetermined: it most plausibly names M. Nissim Bernard, whose boasted acquaintance with M. de Marsantes turns out true for once, but it could name M. de Marsantes as the habitual liar; the two readings place the ironic discredit on different men, so the small praise of Nissim Bernard is left unscored.

Saint-Loup's humiliation is given only as the narrator's apprehension (« Je craignais qu’… il ne fût humilié vis-à-vis de moi ») about a scene outside this passage, so a diminishment of Robert is possible but not asserted by the text and is not scored here.
